{{nihongo|'''Aoi Shrine'''|青渭神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

{{commons category|Category:Aoi-jinja}}
[[ja:青渭神社]]

{{wikidata link|Q11662605|commons|Category:Aoi-jinja|ja|青渭神社|grok=none|check_date=2026-05-28}}

== Japanese content ==
{{Source citation needed|date=July 26, 2015 (Sun) 07:00 (UTC)}}
'''Aoi Shrine''' (あおいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in the former {{ill|Tama district|ja|多摩郡|ko|다마군|zh|多摩郡|qid=Q11430789}} of {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}, {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}. It is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as “Aoi Shrine, Tama District, Musashi Province,” but there are three shrines regarded as candidate sites ({{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}}) of the Engishiki Aoi Shrine: those in {{ill|Higashinaganuma, Inagi City|ja|東長沼|qid=Q30923484}}, {{ill|Jindaiji Motomachi|ja|深大寺元町|qid=Q97172837}}, and {{ill|Sawai|ja|沢井 (青梅市)|qid=Q112152778|lt=Sawai}}.

=== Aoi Shrine in Inagi City ===
{{Shrine
|Name   = Aoi Shrine<br />(Inagi City, Tokyo)
|Image  = [[File:Aoi Shinto Shrine in Inagi in 2009.jpg|250px]]<br />Haiden (April 2009)<br />{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=250|coord={{coord|35|38|33.7|N|139|30|4.2|E}}}}
|Location = {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}{{ill|Inagi|Q317847|qid=Q317847}}{{ill|Higashinaganuma|ja|東長沼|qid=Q30923484}} 1053
|Coordinates = {{coord|35|38|33.7|N|139|30|4.2|E|display=inline}}

It is located at 1053 Higashinaganuma, Inagi City, Tokyo{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Inagi City}}, about a five-minute walk from {{ill|Inagi-Naganuma Station|it|Stazione di Inagi-Naganuma|ja|稲城長沼駅|ko|이나기나가누마역|my|အိနဂိ - နဂနုမဘူတာ|ur|اناگی-ناگانوما اسٹیشن|zh|稻城長沼站|qid=Q5366278}} on the JR {{ill|Nambu Line|de|Nambu-Linie|eo|Linio Nambu|es|Línea Nambu|fa|خط نامبو|fr|Ligne Nambu|id|Jalur Nambu|it|Linea Nambu|ja|南武線|ko|난부선|ru|Линия Намбу|tl|Linyang Nambu|tr|Nambu Hattı|vi|Tuyến Nambu|zh|南武線|qid=Q1366263}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

The enshrined deities are Aoi-no-Kami, {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|Q462803|qid=Q462803|lt=Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto}}{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Inagi City}}. As suggested by the place name “Naganuma,” this area was a {{ill|Floodplain|als|Flussaue|ar|سهل فيضي|ba|Һыубаҫар туғай|bat_smg|Atlajė|be|Пойма|be_x_old|Абалона|bg|Заливна тераса|bh|कछार|bn|প্লাবনভূমি|ca|Plana d'inundació|ckb|دەشتی لافاوی|cs|Údolní niva|cv|Ейӳ (юханшыв лапамĕн пайĕ)|da|Flodslette|de|Flussaue|din|Toc|eml|Barlaida|eo|Apudrivera ebenaĵo|es|Llanura de inundación|et|Lamm|eu|Uholde-lautada|fa|سیلاب‌دشت|fi|Tulvatasanko|fr|Lit majeur|gd|Morbhach|gl|Chaira de inundación|ha|Filin Ambaliyar|he|מישור הצפה|hi|पूरभूमि|ht|Plenn inondab|hy|Գետահովիտ|id|Dataran banjir|it|Golena|ja|氾濫原|ka|ჭალა|kk|Жайылма|ko|범람원|kw|Fennva|ky|Жайылма|la|Vallis vere inundata|lt|Salpa|lv|Paliene|mk|Плавно земјиште|mr|पूर मैदान|myv|Согра|new|न्हसिबुँ|nl|Riviervlakte|nn|Elveslette|no|Elveslette|oc|Plan d'inondacion|pl|Terasa zalewowa|pt|Planície de inundação|ro|Luncă (formă de relief)|ru|Пойма|simple|Floodplain|sl|Poplavna ravnica|sr|Poplavna ravnica|sv|Flodslätt|tr|Taşkın yatağı|tt|Тугай|uk|Заплава|uz|Suv toshqini|vi|Bãi bồi|war|Barahaon na sagka|xmf|ჭალე|zh|河漫滩|zh_yue|氾濫平原|qid=Q193110}} of the {{ill|Tama River|Q1063006|qid=Q1063006}} and had long been marshland. Accordingly, the shrine was formerly also called Ōnuma Myōjin or Aonuma Daimyōjin. Both this Naganuma area and Jindaiji are places closely associated with water, and Aoi-no-Kami is considered to be a {{ill|Suijin|Q3137449|qid=Q3137449}}.

The date of establishment is unknown, but tradition holds that it was founded during the {{ill|Kōnin (era)|de|Kōnin (Ära)|es|Kōnin (era)|fa|کونین (دوره)|fr|Ère Kōnin|ia|Konin (era)|id|Kōnin|ja|弘仁|ko|고닌|ru|Конин (нэнго)|simple|Kōnin (era)|sr|Конин (ера)|tr|Kōnin (dönem)|uk|Конін (ненґо)|zh|弘仁|zh_yue|弘仁|qid=Q1373070}} era (810–824). The current {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine buildings}} are reinforced {{ill|Concrete|Q22657|qid=Q22657}} structures built in {{ill|1974|Q2478|qid=Q2478}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 49), while the main sanctuary housed within the protective hall is believed to have been constructed in the early {{ill|17th century|Q7016|qid=Q7016}}.

There are two pairs (four in total) of {{ill|Komainu|Q20155846|qid=Q20155846}}. On the reverse side of the pair closer to the main sanctuary (shown in the photo on the right) is an inscription reading “{{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}} 13” ({{ill|1830|ab|1830|af|1830|als|1830|am|1830 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1830|ar|1830|ary|1830|arz|1830|ast|1830|avk|1830|az|1830|azb|۱۸۳۰ (میلادی)|ba|1830 йыл|ban|1830|bar|1830|bat_smg|1830|bcl|1830|be|1830|be_x_old|1830|bg|1830|bn|১৮৩০|bpy|মারি ১৮৩০|br|1830|bs|1830.|ca|1830|cdo|1830 nièng|ce|1830 шо|ceb|1830|ckb|١٨٣٠|crh|1830|cs|1830|csb|1830|cv|1830|cy|1830|da|1830|de|1830|diq|1830|el|1830|eml|1830|eo|1830|es|1830|et|1830|eu|1830|fa|۱۸۳۰|fi|1830|fiu_vro|1830|fo|1830|fr|1830|frp|1830|frr|1830|fur|1830|fy|1830|ga|1830|gag|1830|gan|1830年|gcr|1830|gd|1830|gl|1830|gv|1830|hak|1830-ngièn|he|1830|hi|१८३०|hr|1830.|hsb|1830|ht|1830 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1830|hy|1830|hyw|1830 թուական|ia|1830|id|1830|ilo|1830|io|1830|is|1830|it|1830|ja|1830年|jbo|1830moi|jv|1830|ka|1830|kaa|1830|kk|1830 жыл|kn|೧೮೩೦|ko|1830년|krc|1830 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1830|kv|1830-ӧд во|la|1830|lb|1830|lez|1830 йис|li|1830|lij|1830|lld|1830|lmo|1830|lt|1830 m.|lv|1830. gads|mai|१८३०|map_bms|1830|mdf|1830|mg|1830|mhr|1830|mi|1830|min|1830|mk|1830|mr|इ.स. १८३०|mrj|1830 и|ms|1830|my|၁၈၃၀|myv|1830 ие|mzn|۱۸۳۰|nah|1830|nap|1830|nds|1830|new|ई सं १८३०|nl|1830|nn|1830|no|1830|nrm|1830|nso|1830|oc|1830|olo|1830|or|୧୮୩୦|os|1830-æм аз|pap|1830|pl|1830|pnb|1830|pt|1830|qu|1830|ro|1830|ru|1830 год|rue|1830|sa|१८३०|sah|1830|sc|1830|scn|1830|sd|1830ع|se|1830|sh|1830.|shn|1830|si|1830|simple|1830|sk|1830|sl|1830|smn|1830|sq|1830|sr|1830|stq|1830|su|1830|sv|1830|sw|1830|szl|1830|ta|1830|te|1830|tg|Соли 1830|th|พ.ศ. 2373|tk|1830|tl|1830|tly|1830|tpi|1830|tr|1830|tt|1830 ел|ug|1830 - يىلى|uk|1830|ur|1830ء|uz|1830|vec|1830|vi|1830|vls|1830|vo|1830|wa|1830|war|1830|wuu|1830年|xmf|1830|yi|1830|za|1830 nienz|zea|1830|zh|1830年|zh_classical|一八三〇年|zh_min_nan|1830 nî|zh_yue|1830年|qid=Q7576}}). The other pair bears an inscription from the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} period.

The shrine grounds are long and narrow from north to south. Although nearby spec houses using modern building materials detract from the atmosphere, venerable old trees remain, conveying the sense of an ancient sacred precinct. According to elderly locals who remember the past, countless large trees once grew densely here, making it dark even at midday.

At the grand festival, a {{ill|Lion dance|Q713866|qid=Q713866}} known as the “Aoi Shishimai” is dedicated.

=== Aoi Shrine in Chōfu City ===
{{Shrine
|Name = Aoi Shrine<br />(Chōfu City, Tokyo)
|Image = [[File:Aoi-jinja in Chofu 01 - Jan 1, 2019.jpg|250px]]<br />Haiden (January 2019)<br />{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=250|coord={{coord|35|40|2|N|139|33|10.8|E}}}}
|Location = {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}{{ill|Chōfu|Q210667|qid=Q210667}}{{ill|Jindaiji Motomachi|ja|深大寺元町|qid=Q97172837}} 5-17-10
|Coordinates = {{coord|35|40|2|N|139|33|10.8|E|display=inline}}
|Enshrined deity = Aoi Ōkami{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Chōfu City}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aonuma Manuma Oshihime-no-Kami}})
|Shrine rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}; former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}
|Established = Unknown{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Chōfu City}}
|Annual festival = Second Sunday of October
}}
{{Main|The Zelkova of Aoi Shrine}}
It is located at 5-17-10 Jindaiji Motomachi, Chōfu City, Tokyo{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Chōfu City}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Chōfu City}}.

Although the date of establishment is unknown, it has long been revered as the chief {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=tutelary shrine}} of the Jindaiji area. In the past, it possessed shrine lands exceeding five chō. Within the grounds there was a large pond fed by spring water, which shimmered with blue waves; hence it was also called Aonami Tenjin Shrine. It has deep ties with {{ill|Jindai-ji (Tokyo)|Q500736|qid=Q500736}}.

The enshrined deity, Aoi Ōkami, is identified with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aonuma Manuma Oshihime-no-Kami}}, and it is also said that the shrine worshiped a great serpent dwelling in the large pond. In any case, it may safely be regarded as a water deity.

The {{ill|Shinboku|Q48743901|qid=Q48743901}}, the {{ill|great zelkova of Aoi Shrine|Q24868795|qid=Q24868795}}, is a giant tree recorded in works such as the {{ill|Edo meisho zue|Q2704637|qid=Q2704637}} and is designated a {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}} of the city.
{{clear}}

=== Aoi Shrine in Ōme City ===
{{Shrine
|Name=Aoi Shrine<br />(Ōme City, Tokyo)
|Image=[[File:Sougakusan jinja.JPG|250px]]<br />Okumiya at the summit of Mount Sōgaku<br />{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=10|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=250|coord={{coord|35|48|32.3|N|139|11|1.6|E}}}}
|Location={{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}{{ill|Ōme, Tokyo|Q237683|qid=Q237683}} Sawai 3-chōme 1060 {{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Ōme City}}
|Coordinates = {{coord|35|48|32.3|N|139|11|1.6|E|display=inline}}
|Enshrined deity={{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Ōme City}}
|Shrine rank={{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Ōme City}}; former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}
|Established=Unknown
|Annual festival=April 18 (or the nearest Sunday){{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Ōme City}}
}}
[[File:Aoi jinja izumi.JPG|thumb|left|200px|Aoi no I, near the summit of Mount Sōgaku]]
The shrine has its inner sanctuary (okumiya) at the summit of {{ill|Mount Sōgaku|Q11492964|qid=Q11492964}} in Ōme City, Tokyo (Sawai 3-chōme 1060), and its village shrine (satomiya) at Sawai 3-chōme 639. Its former shrine rank was Gōsha. The principal enshrined deity is {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}.

Near the summit of Mount Sōgaku is a sacred spring known as Mana-i{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Ōme City}}. It is also called Aoi no I (“Well of Aoi”) and is said to be the origin of the shrine’s name.

The date of establishment is unknown, but according to shrine tradition, in the 7th year of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, when an epidemic spread throughout the country, the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|Q208233|qid=Q208233}} prayed to the deities in various regions and donated sacred land to this shrine, where rites were performed. It is said that during the {{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} era (938–947), {{ill|Minamoto no Tsunemoto|Q3099236|qid=Q3099236}} constructed shrine buildings. The present shrine buildings were rebuilt in the 2nd year of {{ill|Kōka|Q1325317|qid=Q1325317}}.

In the early {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} period, a worship hall was built at the foot of Mount Sōgaku and designated as a distant worship hall{{sfn|Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines, Ōme City}}. Today, the main shrine at the summit is treated as the inner sanctuary, while the distant worship hall at the mountain’s base serves as the village shrine, where festivals and rites are conducted.
